# Objective
Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events, with devastating impacts. This analysis will identify and visualize the impacts of the February 2021 Texas power crisis — caused by a series three of extreme winter storms — by estimating the number of homes in the Houston metropolitan area that lost power and investigate whether not these impacts were disproportionately felt.

This analysis is based on remotely-sensed night lights data, acquired from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) onboard the Suomi satellite. In particular, we use the VNP46A1 to detect differences in night lights before and after the storm to identify areas that lost electric power. To determine the number of homes that lost power, we spatially join these areas with OpenStreetMap data on buildings and roads.

Produce: 
- a set of maps comparing night light intensities before and after the first two storms
- a map of the homes in Houston that lost power
- an estimate of the number of homes in Houston that lost power
- a brief reflection (approx. 100 words) summarizing your results and discussing any limitations to this study
- ADD CRS CHECKS/WARNINGS

## Merge data

```{r}
# Merge tile data for Feb 7 and Feb 16

tx7 <- st_mosaic(feb7_tile5, feb7_tile6)
tx16 <- st_mosaic(feb16_tile5, feb16_tile6)
```

```{r}
# Check if crs matches
st_crs(roads) == st_crs(houses)
st_crs(tx7) == st_crs(tx16)
st_crs(tx7) == st_crs(houses)
```

# Workflow 

## Step 1: find locations that experienced a blackout by creating a mask

```{r}
# Find the difference in night light between the two dates 
light_diff <- tx7 - tx16

# Subset
blackouts <- light_diff
blackouts[blackouts < 200] <- NA

# Crop to the Houston area 
box <- st_bbox(
  c(xmin = -96.5, ymin = 29, xmax = -94.5, ymax = 30.5),
  crs = st_crs(4326))

houston_crop <- st_crop(blackouts, box) 

# Vectorize the blackout mask, fix invalid geometries, reproject crs
blackout_vect <- st_as_sf(houston_crop, merge = TRUE) |>
  st_make_valid() |> 
  st_transform(crs = 3083)
```


## Step 2: exclude highways from analysis

```{r}
# Check that crs 3083 units are meters
st_crs(blackout_vect)$units

# Reproject roads CRS to match reprojected blackout, create a 200m buffer around highways
highway_buffer <- roads |> 
  st_transform(crs = 3083) |> 
  st_buffer(dist = 200) |> 
  st_union()

# Exclude locations within 200m of highways 
blackout_no_hwy <- st_difference(blackout_vect, highway_buffer)

plot(blackout_no_hwy)
```

## Step 3: identify homes that experienced blackouts by combining the locations of homes and blackouts

```{r}
# Reproject houses crs to match
houses <- st_transform(houses, crs = 3083)

# Spatially join homes data with blackout data
home_blackouts <- st_filter(x = blackout_no_hwy, y = houses, .predicate = st_intersects)
nrow(home_blackouts) # The number of houses that experienced a blackout 
```

# Visualizations
Maps comparing night light intensities before and after the first two storms

```{r}
# Crop to the Houston area 
tx7_crop <- st_crop(tx7, box) 
tx16_crop <- st_crop(tx16, box) 

# Plot
light_before_after <- c(tx7_crop, tx16_crop)
names(light_before_after) <- c("2-07-2021", "2-16-2021")
plot(merge(light_before_after))
```
